question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[k,11k],$ where $k$ is a positive number, compute $P(0<X<6k).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[k,11k],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10k},\, & k\le x\le 11k, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X<6k) & =P(k<X<6k) \\  & ={\int }_{k}^{6k}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{k}^{6k}\frac{1}{10k}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{6k-k}{10k} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
